title: Setup & Python Fundamentals for AI Agents
why: Every autonomous AI agent starts with Python scripts interacting with OS processes, shell commands, virtual environments, and package managers. You need an isolated environment so dependencies like Pydantic, LangChain, or OpenAI SDK don't collide.
objectives: Set up fast virtual environments using venv or uv
Configure environment variables and dependency managers
Execute your first tool-calling test harness script
concept:
**Why UV over standard PIP?**
uv is an extremely fast Python package manager written in Rust. When developing multi-agent systems with dozens of libraries, uv installs packages up to 10-100x faster than standard pip.

Virtual environments isolate project-specific dependencies. Never install agent packages directly into system Python to prevent breaking system tools.

code.content:
# Check python version
python --version

# Create virtual environment with uv or python venv
python -m venv .venv

# Activate on Windows:
# .venv\Scripts\activate
# Activate on Linux/macOS:
# source .venv/bin/activate

# Install core agent dependencies
pip install requests pydantic python-dotenv

practice.description: Create a virtual environment named .venv, activate it, and write a Python script that outputs current python interpreter path and checks if python-dotenv is installed.
practice.hint: Use sys.executable to inspect the running python binary path.

requirements: Check OS name, CPU architecture, and Python runtime version
Output formatted JSON report ready to be parsed by an LLM

checklist: Understood why venv isolation is required for AI agents
mistakes: Installing packages globally without activating the virtual environment
Using outdated Python versions (< 3.10) that do not support modern type union operators (|)
